messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: anomalous KV prefetch growth detected for svc-inference-prod in us-west-2. Prefetch count increased 3.8x over 10m, eviction rate spiking, continuous-batcher latency tail rising. Auto-severity: P1. thread:2245678901
sarah (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Noticed increased paging and a few streaming stalls in the dashboard. Setting up a quick coord room. @mike @juan please priority.
mike (infra): Looking at node metrics now. Eviction-rate spike correlates w/ heavy prefix prefetch. Could be runaway prefetch for longer contexts. I can throttle prefetch on the fly via feature-flag. Suggest setting kv.prefetch.factor -> 0.25 as a first pass.
juan (runtime): Possible regression from last week's continuous-batching change — we relaxed batch cadence to help throughput, that can amplify prefetch. Also seeing a partial-flush path in streaming that's hitting an off-by-one with KV paging. If prefetch and batch cadence align badly we get micro-bursts + eviction.
sarah (oncall): Plan: 1) throttle prefetch to 0.25 feature-flag 2) reduce continuous batch window to 8ms for canary nodes 3) temporarily disable streaming partial-flush path (stream.partial_flush=false) to stop cadence stalls. Mike/juan can you execute; I'll update support and customers.
mike (infra): Running prefetch throttle: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags -d '{"kv.prefetch.factor":0.25}'` -> 202 accepted. Pushing to canary pool first.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: flags/kv-prefetch-throttle -> canary nodes (5) at 2245678923. CI: ok.
juan (runtime): Pushing runtime config for batch window and partial-flush to canary: `batch.window_ms=8` and `stream.partial_flush=false`. Patch:```diff
- batch.window_ms=16
- stream.partial_flush=true
+ batch.window_ms=8
+ stream.partial_flush=false
``` Applying to canary.
mike (infra): Canary metrics 60s in: eviction-rate down 48% on canary, tail latency 95p down ~120ms, token cadence stalls reduced. No increase in downstream error rate so far.
sarah (oncall): Good. Ellie, can you surface customer impact and push initial comms to support? We'll keep canary for 10m and then ramp if stable.
ellie (support): On it. Triage summary for ops: "Users on dedicated and private clusters experienced increased 5xx on streaming during 22:08-22:26 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~18k, impacted customers: 6 (IDs: cust-407, cust-998, cust-appletrial, cust-fin-2, cust-saasx, cust-beta). Support message draft: ‘Investigating increased streaming errors; mitigation in progress. Will follow up with timeline.’
juan (runtime): Canary 5m stable. I'll start a controlled ramp of the flags to 40% nodes. Watch for paging and token cadence metrics.
mike (infra): Ramp to 40% at 2245678999 -> metrics: eviction trending down cluster-wide, but noticed a small uptick in short 502s from the streaming ingress path on one AZ. Investigating ingress LB health.
ops-sre: FYI saw the 502s — they map to a proxy timeout when backend flush is transiently delayed. That's probably from partial-flush being toggled; some clients hit the toggled-inflight code path. Recommend keep partial_flush off and increase streaming request timeout at LB by +200ms temporarily.
sarah (oncall): Agreed. Juan, can you coordinate with ops-sre to bump the LB timeout? Mike can you watch client retries?
juan (runtime): Changing LB timeout: `kubectl patch svc streaming-ingress -p '{"spec":{"timeoutSeconds":35}}'` -> will apply to AZ1 then AZ2. Patching now.
deploy-bot: LB timeout patch applied to AZ1 at 2245679017, AZ2 at 2245679028.
mike (infra): Client retries look normal, error rate falling back to baseline. By 2245679035 overall 5xx down to pre-incident levels, token cadence stable on 95p.
sarah (oncall): Excellent. Next steps: keep flags at new values for 24h, open a follow-up PR to fix partial-flush bug (juan + runtime team). Assign postmortem. Ellie please update support with ETA and affected customer list; CC account execs for enterprise customers.
ellie (support): Sent support update to affected accounts and created follow-up ticket INC-2245679. Drafted customer-facing note: "We mitigated an internal prefetch/batching regression causing intermittent streaming errors; continuing monitoring; root cause investigation underway"
ops-sre: Creating incident ticket with key artifacts (heap/eviction graphs, canary diffs, flag changes, deploy logs). See /incidents/2245678901/artifacts in Confluence.
sarah (oncall): Handoff: I'm going to start the formal postmortem doc. @mike you have the night oncall for follow-up monitoring, escalate to me if any reappearance. Action items: (1) runtime: fix partial-flush off-by-one (PR by EOD) (2) infra: add a safe-limit for kv.prefetch.factor to avoid >1x runaway (3) support: customer follow-ups + RCA template.
mike (infra): Ack. I'll keep an eye on eviction-rate alert and rollback flag if it flares.
jun (note): (typo) -> juan (runtime)
sarah (oncall): Closing thread summary: mitigation applied (prefetch throttle + reduced batch window + partial-flush disabled + LB timeout bump), metrics restored, impacted customers notified. Will schedule postmortem in ops channel tomorrow. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident 2245678901 marked resolved at 2245679057. Auto-generated ticket INC-2245679 created for postmortem and follow-ups.
